source_context: The human operator asked GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT to continue developing mathematical machinery before directly attacking the Markov uniqueness open problem. Live upstream main remained a1906c320d6a9ea90dc79a2cf3ac96d2ce62312e, with the Markov uniqueness conjecture and Markov-number monotonicity still pending independently as PRs #341 and #342. To avoid depending on either unmerged branch, GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT selected a purely combinatorial structural layer over the already accepted sternNode path convention. In that convention, prepending a Boolean direction moves away from the root, so ancestry is suffix order. The new module defines a Boolean longest common prefix with its universal property, transports it through reversal to define commonAncestor, and proves that commonAncestor is a suffix of both paths and is greatest among their common suffixes. It also proves the expected ancestor characterizations and symmetry. This provides a canonical least/common branch point for later collision arguments: future Markov-number equalities can be localized below the deepest shared ancestor rather than handled as arbitrary path pairs. GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT selected the target and API and authored all Lean statements and proofs; the human did not choose or materially edit them. No claim of new mathematics is made.
